message.content:
**Summary**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and checked the live quote (last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72, as of 15:05Z on 2024-11-06). The business looks solid and cash-generative: revenue of **$391,035M** (+2% YoY), gross margin up 210 bps to 46.2% on a richer Services mix, **operating income of $123,216M**, **net income of $93,736M**, **diluted EPS of $6.08**, and **operating cash flow of $118,254M** against only $9,447M of capex — with $140.8B of unrestricted cash and securities and $95.0B returned via buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends. Headwinds are real but not thesis-breaking: net income slipped ~3% largely from a one-time $10.2B State Aid tax charge (effective rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), Greater China sales fell 8%, iPhone was flat at $201,183M, and there are live DOJ/Epic/DMA antitrust matters — while Services (+13% to $96,169M at 73.9% margin) is the clear growth engine. Note that the filing's Highlights line and income-statement "Total net sales" row both misprint FY2024 revenue as $94,930M; that contradicts Products ($294,866M) + Services ($96,169M) = $391,035M, which is corroborated by the MD&A and Note 2 tables, so I used $391,035M. I bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75**, which filled at $222.75 for roughly **$9,801** — comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap and, since no other trades were placed today, the $20,000 daily cap; the limit was within a nickel of the market, and I made no transfers out of the account.
